answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by charging a proof-of-work price for every new identity. Before trading, an agent must solve a fresh, verifiable puzzle tied to its public key, like a raven proving it flew the distance rather than merely claiming wings. The puzzle is cheap for one honest newcomer, but it punishes a comet-like burst of thousands of hollow sock puppets, since each fake identity costs its own computation and time. An attacker must spend real hardware and electricity per identity, so flooding stops paying.
